headline: Majors overbought and crowded long, but whale flow shows a split: ETH to cold storage, BTC to exchanges, stablecoins flat despite greed at 73.
paragraphs: Every major is above its 200-day line, but none has reclaimed the golden cross. BTC sits 36.8% below its 12-month peak, ETH 48.1%, and the entire cohort is underwater relative to recent highs, yet RSI readings are extreme: BTC at 82, ETH at 79.4, SOL at 85, XRP at 80.9, BNB at 84.5. These are overbought by textbook definition. MACD is above signal on all seven assets, which tells you momentum has not yet rolled over, but momentum this extended against trend this extended (coins well below their annual peaks) is the setup where a small friction event can trigger quick repricing. ADA alone sits below its 200-day, and its RSI at 68.8 is the only one shy of extreme, a crack in the consensus. Over the last seven days, BTC is up 25.19%, ETH up 31.83%, SOL up 28.26%, and XRP has nearly doubled at 48.46%, yet the 24-hour moves are all modest: the surge is already in the tape, not arriving. That matters.

Derivatives positioning reflects the greed: perp funding is positive across the board, ranging from BTC at 0.007% per 8 hours (annualizing to 7.7%) through ETH, SOL, XRP at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized). Longs are paying to hold. Open interest is substantial, BTC at $2.32 billion, ETH at $1.48 billion, but the crowding is most severe in the small-caps. DOGE shows a 3.55-to-1 long-to-short ratio, XRP at 2.12-to-1, SOL at 1.89-to-1. These are skewed bets. Over the last 9 to 24 hours, liquidations are running heavy on the long side: BTC saw $7.0 million in long liquidations against $5.5 million in shorts, but ETH skewed far worse at $10.7 million longs to $4.8 million shorts. SOL, XRP, and DOGE are all liquidating far more longs than shorts, which is consistent with a crowd that got long on the move and is now getting tested. The tape shows tension: the bet is crowded, it is expensive to hold, and the small moves in price are already shaking out the marginal holders.

Whale flow over the last 24 hours was net $110.8 million off exchanges, but the composition tells the real story. ETH moved $146 million off exchanges (to cold storage, almost certainly), while BTC moved $35.2 million net onto exchanges. This is not a unified show of hands. The biggest single moves were ETH leaving Binance ($146 million out), BTC leaving Binance ($117.8 million out), and then, crucially, $96 million of BTC flowing onto OKEx. Stablecoin inflows to Binance totaled $236.6 million (USDC and USDT combined), which is dry powder staged but not yet spent. The weekly picture deepens the tension: in the week ending August 3rd, $1.128 billion moved off exchanges. Since then, the trend has reversed. The week ending August 10th saw $544 million move onto exchanges, August 17th another $49 million on, and the week ending August 24th (still in progress) shows $887 million moving onto exchanges. That reversal from off to on, building now, is the opposite of a conviction move. Whales are taking ETH to cold storage, which reads as conviction, while staging stablecoins on the exchange and allowing BTC to flow back in. That is not one message.

Fear and Greed stands at 73, 'Greed', and the 30-day range from 25 to 73 shows the gauge has swung hard. The crowd is confident. Aggregate market cap fell 0.72% on the day despite the bulk of the index up, which suggests breadth is failing: the gainers are a small set pulling the aggregate higher, but the median asset is pulling lower. BTC dominance at 59.1% is stable but shows Bitcoin has not reasserted the lead; the move is driven by alts. Total stablecoin float at $308.6 billion is essentially flat month-on-month, growing only 0.01%, which means the dry powder is not expanding into greed. There is no new money flowing in to fuel the extension. Realized volatility remains high across the board (BTC at 43.6%, ETH at 70%, XRP at 81.5%, DOGE at 64.4%), which tells you the moves are not smooth; price is jerking, and that jerking is triggering stops and cascades.

Watch for three things. First, whether perp funding holds positive or begins to flip negative: a flip from longs paying to hold to shorts paying would be an early signal that the crowd has stopped believing. Second, whether BTC can reclaim the golden cross; right now it is above the 200-day but below both the 50-day and the 200-day, a lag, and closing a candle with both 50 above 200 would be a regime confirmation that even the optimists have not yet declared. Right now the trend is up, but the structure is weak. Third, whether stablecoin float begins to rise: $308.6 billion flat is a ceiling, and if that number stays there while the whale flows shift onto exchanges, it means the buying power is staged but not being deployed, which would be a warning that the crowd's dry powder is not actually moving at this price. The tape says the move is extended, the bet is crowded, and the real money has a split personality. One more day of this will tell you whether the greed holds or the momentum rolls.
